financials_interim.notes: Same source as GROUP row (source_id 52519), Company column of the same statements. LVEF (Company, standalone) is a pure holding entity: Revenue and Direct expenses are both '-' for both periods -- it earns no trading revenue of its own, only investment-type income (interest income, other income) and its share of associate profits (156,380k vs 384,510k PY, via 'Investment in equity accounted investees' on the Company balance sheet, which includes what are subsidiaries at Group level, since Company-only accounts do not consolidate). revenue and cost_of_sales/gross_profit intentionally left NULL (not blank/zero) for this basis, reflecting a genuine 'not applicable' structure rather than a zero-revenue operating result -- operating_profit=(13,126)k is a pure holding-cost operating loss (admin/other opex only, no revenue to offset). finance_income=207k (interest income only). PBT 82,376k = PAT 82,376k = profit attributable to equity holders at Group level exactly (Company IS the ultimate parent, no NCI at Company level), confirming internal consistency. EPS 0.11 = 82,376k / 766,353,136 shares, same denominator as Group (single listed entity). shares_in_issue, cash_from_operations/investing/financing, capex, and balance-sheet fields per Company column, p.4 and p.7. trade_receivables/trade_payables/inventory left NULL for the same disclosure-gap reason as the Group row.

Source: LVL Energy Fund PLC interim FS for quarter ended 30 Jun 2026 (signed 13 Aug 2026, unaudited). P&L p.3 (doc p.01), Balance Sheet p.4 (doc p.02), Statement of Changes in Equity p.5-6 (doc p.03-04), Cash Flow p.7 (doc p.05), Notes p.8-9 (doc p.06-07). GROUP basis judgment: LVEF is NOT a literal closed-end NAV fund -- despite the 'Fund' name, the Group consolidates a handful of operating subsidiaries (Lanka Energy International, Unit Energy Lanka, Sapthakanya Hydro, Campion Hydro, Pupulaketiya Hydro, Solar Energy Investments entities) that generate real trading Revenue (107,804k) less Direct expenses (48,782k) = Gross Profit 59,022k -- a conventional P&L structure, not fair-value/NAV movements. Separately, LVEF holds a portfolio of equity-accounted associate power plants (Hayleys Hydro, the Bangladesh associates Lakdhanavi Bangla Power & Feni Lanka Power, etc.) whose income is picked up as one line, 'Share of earnings from equity accounted investees' (153,418k vs 387,823k PY) -- this is NOT part of revenue/gross profit and is mapped to no FINANCIAL_FIELDS slot; it flows straight into PBT. revenue=107,804k is the Group's own trading revenue only (subsidiaries), explicitly excluding the associate share-of-profit line -- flagged so it is not mistaken for a fund total-income figure. operating_profit = 'Results from operating activities' = 40,063k (Revenue+interest/other income-opex, before associate share and finance cost). finance_income = Interest income only (1,007k); 'Other income' (286k) is not separately mapped (no slot) -- both are visible on p.3 if needed. depreciation_amortization = Depreciation (20,402k) + Amortization of intangibles (1,281k) per CF statement, combined = 21,683k. minority_interest = NCI share of profit (19,958k). trade_receivables / inventory / trade_payables left NULL: this holding/fund-structured group's balance sheet has no line items so-labelled -- current assets are 'Loans and receivables' (126,004k) and 'Other receivables' (1,056,168k), and current liabilities show only 'Other payables' (19,672k) with no purchases-ledger trade payables disclosed; mapping either to trade_receivables/trade_payables would be a guess not supported by the document, so left blank as a genuine disclosure gap rather than invented. shares_in_issue=766,353,136 per Note 9 (post rights issue, 3-for-31 at Rs 7.50/share completed May 2026, raising Rs 507,145,455 -- see Note 6, doc p.07). EPS basic cross-checked: 82,376k / 766,353,136 = Rs 0.1075 rounds to disclosed Rs 0.11. eps_diluted left NULL -- filing discloses only 'Basic earnings per share', no diluted figure or dilutive instruments mentioned. cash_from_operations = Net cash from operating activities (-370,466k, i.e. net of tax and interest paid; before working-capital changes it was +47,257k -- the deep negative reflects Interest paid of 380,573k, itself driven by the short-term bridge borrowing below). capex = 0 for this quarter (PP&E additions line shows '-'; PY comparative was -1,701k). Cross-check: PBT reconciles bottom-up -- 59,022 (GP) + 1,007 (interest inc) + 286 (other inc) - 353 (S&E exp) - 19,899 (other opex) = 40,063 (op. result); + 153,418 (associate share) - 83,264 (finance cost) = 110,217 (PBT). Matches printed PBT exactly -- no column-order artifact found on this statement.

thesis.company_name: L V L Energy Fund PLC
thesis.thesis_text: LVL Energy Fund PLC (LVEF) is a renewable-energy holding group whose consolidated hydro/solar operating subsidiaries performed steadily in Q1 FY2026/27 (Revenue -8% YoY to Rs.107.80mn, operating margin improving to 37.2% from 36.8%), but whose Group PBT and PAT collapsed 69% and 71% YoY to Rs.110.22mn and Rs.102.33mn because equity-accounted income from its associate power-plant portfolio (including two Bangladesh entities) fell 60% YoY, a Rs.234.41mn drop explaining 93.6% of the total decline. The filing discloses no per-associate breakdown, so it cannot be determined how much of this reflects genuine operating weakness at the associates versus a disclosed accounting policy change to recognise delayed Bangladesh Power Development Board interest income on a cash-received rather than accrual basis. A 3-for-31 Rights Issue completed in May 2026 raised Rs.507.15mn, applied entirely to debt paydown at the parent (Lanka Ventures PLC) and two bank lenders -- a genuine deleveraging step. At Rs.6.50, P/B of ~0.69x looks statistically cheap against Group equity of Rs.7,203.8mn, but annualised run-rate P/E of ~14.8x on this quarter's depressed EPS is not, and no dividend data exists to anchor a yield case. With only one interim quarter on file and the associate-income decline unexplained, this thesis should be revisited once a second quarter clarifies the trend (Interim Financial Statements, source_doc_id 52519, p.3-4).
thesis.gaps_note: Macro & Industry Outlook (10% weight) unavailable -- no Sri Lanka/Bangladesh power-sector tariff or regulatory data source exists in this project; the remaining five pillars are renormalized to sum to 100% (Financial Quality 33.3%, Growth 22.2%, Valuation 22.2%, Business Quality 16.7%, Governance & Risk 5.6%). Confidence is limited: only ONE interim quarter is on file (no annual report review, no multi-period trend), no dividend data exists for LVEF, prior-year comparatives are restated without disclosed quantum, and the single largest driver of this quarter's results (a 60% fall in associate income) has no per-associate breakdown to verify.

financial_quality.rationale: LVL Energy Fund PLC (LVEF) has one interim quarter on file (Q1 FY2026/27). The consolidated operating subsidiaries (hydro/solar generation) held up well -- Revenue fell only 8% YoY to Rs.107.80mn and Gross Profit was almost flat (Rs.59.02mn vs Rs.59.15mn PY), with operating margin actually improving slightly to 37.2% from 36.8%. However, Group PBT and PAT collapsed 69% and 71% YoY (to Rs.110.22mn and Rs.102.33mn) almost entirely because the Group's equity-accounted 'Share of earnings from equity accounted investees' (its associate power-plant portfolio, including two Bangladesh entities) fell 60% YoY to Rs.153.42mn from Rs.387.82mn -- a Rs.234.41mn drop explaining 93.6% of the total PBT decline, with no per-associate breakdown disclosed to isolate the cause. A recently completed 3-for-31 Rights Issue (May 2026, Rs.507.15mn raised) was applied entirely to debt paydown across the parent (Lanka Ventures PLC) and two bank lenders, a genuine balance-sheet-strengthening move, but a Rs.99mn provision against delayed Bangladesh dividend receivables and a disclosed change to recognise delayed BPDB interest income on a cash-received rather than accrual basis add uncertainty to the associate income line going forward.

growth_outlook.rationale: Group PBT, PAT and EPS all fell 69-76% YoY this quarter, driven almost entirely by the associate-income decline described above rather than the consolidated operating subsidiaries, whose revenue and margins were roughly stable. Because the filing gives no per-associate breakdown, it cannot be determined how much of the decline reflects a genuine operating deterioration at the associate power plants versus the disclosed accounting policy change (excluding Rs.213.8mn of delayed BPDB interest income from the equity-accounted share going forward). Basic EPS fell 76% YoY to Rs.0.11 despite a 9.7% increase in shares in issue from the Rights Issue, meaning the profit collapse far outweighed the dilution.

valuation.rationale: At Rs.6.50 (2026-08-31, market cap Rs.4,981.3mn), P/B is approximately 0.69x on Group equity of Rs.7,203.8mn -- statistically cheap and supported by real hydro/solar generation assets and associate power-plant investments. On an annualised run-rate using this quarter's depressed EPS of Rs.0.11 (x4 = Rs.0.44), P/E is approximately 14.8x -- not cheap, and this run-rate is itself built on a quarter where associate income fell 60% YoY, so it may understate normalised earnings power if associate income partially recovers, or overstate it if the decline is structural. No dividend data is on file for LVEF, so no yield support can be assessed.

business_quality.rationale: LVEF is a renewable-energy holding group (Utilities) consolidating several hydro/solar operating subsidiaries alongside a portfolio of equity-accounted associate power plants, including two Bangladesh entities (Lakdhanavi Bangla Power and Feni Lanka Power) exposed to Bangladesh Power Development Board (BPDB) payment timing and USD-linked PPA dynamics. The diversified generation-asset base is a structural positive, and the just-completed Rights Issue used entirely to pay down parent and bank debt signals proactive balance-sheet management, but delayed Bangladesh dividend receipts (with a Rs.99mn provision) and a Note 7 restatement of prior-year comparatives (a preference-share-to-NCI reclassification) point to a business still working through structural and cross-border complexity.

governance_risk.rationale: Rights Issue proceeds were applied transparently and in disclosed amounts to specific lenders, including Rs.262mn to settle debt owed to the 51.46% parent shareholder Lanka Ventures PLC -- a related-party transaction disclosed with reasonable specificity. Prior-year comparatives were restated (Note 7) for a preference-share instrument reclassification at a subsidiary, adding a layer of complexity to YoY comparisons that is disclosed but not quantified. No disclosures/circulars feed exists in this project to independently verify board or ownership changes.

key_reasons: Group PBT/PAT fell 69%/71% YoY (to Rs.110.22mn/Rs.102.33mn), driven almost entirely by a 60% fall in equity-accounted associate power-plant income (Rs.234.41mn drop, 93.6% of the PBT decline) -- the Group's own consolidated hydro/solar subsidiaries held revenue and margins roughly steady

P/B of ~0.69x looks statistically cheap against Rs.7,203.8mn of Group equity, but annualised run-rate P/E of ~14.8x on this quarter's depressed EPS is not cheap, and no dividend data exists to provide yield support

A 3-for-31 Rights Issue (Rs.507.15mn, May 2026) was fully applied to debt paydown at the parent and two bank lenders -- a genuine deleveraging move, but only one interim quarter is on file so there is no trend to confirm the associate-income decline is temporary
watch_factors: The filing discloses no per-associate breakdown for the 60% YoY fall in equity-accounted income -- it is not possible to separate a genuine operating decline at the associate power plants from the disclosed policy change to recognise delayed BPDB interest income (Rs.213.8mn in FY2025/26) on a cash-received rather than accrual basis going forward
A Rs.99mn provision against delayed Bangladesh associate dividend receivables (Note 3) signals ongoing cross-border cash-collection friction worth monitoring
Prior-year comparatives are restated (Note 7, preference-share/NCI reclassification) without disclosure of the restatement's quantum -- YoY figures should be read with this caveat

horizon_notes.6m: Q2 FY2026/27 results will show whether associate-power-plant income stabilises or continues to decline, and whether the Rights Issue's debt paydown lowers finance costs.
horizon_notes.1y: If the associate income drop proves to be mostly the disclosed accounting policy change (moving to cash-basis BPDB interest recognition) rather than an operating decline, PBT could stabilise; if it reflects genuine underperformance at the power plants, further declines are possible.
horizon_notes.3y: Thesis depends on the health of the associate power-plant portfolio, particularly the Bangladesh entities' USD-hedged PPA economics and BPDB payment reliability, which this project cannot independently verify without further disclosure.
horizon_notes.5y: No macro/regulatory data source exists in this project to assess Sri Lankan or Bangladeshi renewable-energy tariff policy over a multi-year horizon.

interim_updates.note_text: LVL Energy Fund PLC (LVEF) reported Group Profit Before Tax of Rs.110.22mn for Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026), down 69% YoY from a restated Rs.360.63mn in Q1 FY2025/26 (PY comparatives were restated per Note 7, reclassifying a Preference Share Agreement at subsidiary Lanka Energy International as an NCI equity instrument). The decline is almost entirely a single line item: 'Share of earnings from equity accounted investees' (LVEF's associate power-plant portfolio -- Hayleys Hydro, Neluwa Cascade, Pawan Danavi, Nala Dhanavi, Raj Lanka Power, and the two Bangladesh associates Lakdhanavi Bangla Power and Feni Lanka Power) fell 60% YoY to Rs.153.42mn from Rs.387.82mn PY, a Rs.234.41mn drop that alone accounts for 93.6% of the Rs.250.41mn YoY PBT decline (reconciliation: -Rs.3.19mn narrower operating result, -Rs.234.41mn associate income drop, -Rs.12.82mn higher finance cost = -Rs.250.41mn PBT change, ties exactly to the printed PBT figures). The filing does NOT disclose a per-associate breakdown for the quarter, so the specific cause (lower hydro generation/PPA tariffs, the Bangladesh associates' USD-hedged PPA dynamics, or delayed-interest recognition timing under Note 5) cannot be isolated -- a genuine and material disclosure gap given this line is the whole story. Note 5 explains that the Bangladesh associates' FY2025/26 full-year results included Rs.213.8mn of the Group's proportionate share of delayed-payment interest income from the Bangladesh Power Development Board (BPDB), which the Group has decided to recognise on a cash-received basis going forward (i.e. excluded from equity-accounted share of profit) -- this is a disclosed policy change that plausibly explains at least part of the associate-income drop, but the filing does not quantify how much of the Rs.234.41mn decline is this policy effect versus a genuine fall in the associates' own operating profit. Note 3 separately discloses delayed dividend receipts from the Bangladesh associates and a Rs.99mn provision against the dividend receivable balance (time-value-of-money, expected to reverse on receipt) -- this appears to be a balance-sheet item (receivable carrying value) rather than part of this quarter's P&L, since the PBT bridge above reconciles exactly without it, but the exact accounting placement is not stated. Group Revenue (the consolidated operating subsidiaries only -- Lanka Energy International, Unit Energy Lanka, Sapthakanya/Campion/Pupulaketiya Hydro, Solar Energy Investments entities -- explicitly excluding the associate share-of-profit line) was Rs.107.80mn, -8% YoY (2025: Rs.117.41mn), while Gross Profit was almost flat, Rs.59.02mn vs Rs.59.15mn PY (-0.2%); operating margin (Results from operating activities / Revenue) actually held up, 37.2% vs 36.8% PY, so none of the PBT decline is an operating-margin story. Finance cost rose 18% YoY to Rs.83.26mn (2025: Rs.70.45mn) -- a secondary drag, 5% of the total PBT decline -- against Interest Bearing Borrowings that swung sharply within the quarter (Rs.2,000mn drawn and Rs.1,917.66mn repaid per the cash flow statement, consistent with a short-term bridge facility). Company-level PBT/PAT (a pure holding entity; Revenue and Direct expenses are both nil) tell the same story in sharper form: down 74% YoY to Rs.82.38mn from Rs.322.77mn PY, with the Company's own share of associate earnings falling 59% to Rs.156.38mn from Rs.384.51mn PY (94.9% of the Company's Rs.240.40mn PBT decline) and the Company's holding-cost operating loss widening 15% to Rs.(13.13)mn from Rs.(11.44)mn PY. Basic EPS fell 76% YoY to Rs.0.11 from Rs.0.46 despite the Company completing a 3-for-31 Rights Issue in May 2026 at Rs.7.50/share (Note 6), raising Rs.507.15mn and increasing shares in issue 9.7% to 766,353,136 from 698,733,742 -- the profit collapse far outweighed the dilution. Rights proceeds were used entirely to settle borrowings: Rs.262mn to Lanka Ventures PLC (the 51.46% parent shareholder), Rs.54.67mn + Rs.28.57mn + Rs.27.78mn of DFCC Bank term-loan capital, and Rs.134.13mn of NDB Bank term-loan capital and interest (Note 6, 100% utilised as at the reporting date).
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: this is LVEF's first financial_statements/interim_updates entry in this DB (no closer prior quarter has been collected). Genuine filing-level gaps: (1) no per-associate breakdown is given for the quarter's 'Share of earnings from equity accounted investees' -- the single line that explains 93.6% (Group) / 94.9% (Company) of the entire YoY PBT decline (Rs.234.41mn / Rs.228.13mn drop) -- so it cannot be determined how much of the fall is lower hydro generation/tariffs at the local associates versus the Bangladesh associates' dynamics versus the Note 5 policy change (excluding delayed BPDB interest income of Rs.213.8mn recognised in FY2025/26 from the equity-accounted share going forward, now on a cash-received basis); (2) the Rs.99mn provision against the Bangladesh dividend receivable (Note 3, time-value-of-money, expected to reverse on receipt) is disclosed without stating which period's P&L or which balance sheet line it sits in -- the PBT bridge in this note reconciles exactly without it, suggesting it is a receivable-carrying-value adjustment already reflected in the opening balance sheet rather than a Q1 FY2026/27 P&L charge, but this is inference, not stated fact; (3) PY comparatives are labelled 'Restated' on the face of the P&L and cash flow statements (Note 7, preference-share-to-NCI reclassification at subsidiary Lanka Energy International) -- this YoY comparison is therefore against a restated PY base, not the originally-reported Q1 FY2025/26 figures, and the quantum of the restatement itself is not separately disclosed in this interim filing; (4) trade_receivables/trade_payables/inventory are not disclosed as distinct balance sheet captions for either basis (see financial_statements notes) -- a genuine structural gap for this holding/fund-structured group, not an omission on our part.
interim_updates.takeaway: LVEF's 69-76% YoY declines across PBT, PAT and EPS are overwhelmingly a single-line story: the Group's equity-accounted share of associate power-plant earnings fell Rs.234.41mn (-60%), accounting for 93.6% of the entire PBT decline, while the Group's own conventional operating business (the consolidated hydro/solar subsidiaries) held revenue and margins broadly steady (-8% revenue, operating margin actually improved to 37.2%). Because the filing gives no per-associate breakdown, it is not possible to determine how much of the associate-income drop reflects a genuine operating deterioration at the associate power plants (including the two Bangladesh associates with USD-hedged PPAs) versus the disclosed accounting policy change to recognise delayed BPDB interest income on a cash-received rather than accrual basis (Note 5) -- this is the single most important item to follow up on with the company. Separately, the successful Rights Issue (Rs.507.15mn raised, fully applied to debt paydown across the parent and two bank lenders) and delayed Bangladesh dividend receipts (Note 3, with a Rs.99mn receivable provision) point to an active balance-sheet and cash-flow management exercise around the associate portfolio that is worth monitoring into subsequent quarters.

Group 'Share of earnings from equity accounted investees' (associate power plants incl. Bangladesh's Lakdhanavi Bangla Power & Feni Lanka Power) fell 60% YoY to Rs.153.42mn from Rs.387.82mn -- a Rs.234.41mn drop that alone explains 93.6% of the Group's Rs.250.41mn YoY PBT decline; Company-level equivalent fell 59% to Rs.156.38mn from Rs.384.51mn.

Group trading Revenue (operating subsidiaries only, excludes associate income) Rs.107.80mn, -8% YoY (2025: Rs.117.41mn); Gross Profit almost flat, Rs.59.02mn vs Rs.59.15mn PY (-0.2%); operating margin improved slightly to 37.2% from 36.8% PY -- the profit decline is not an operating-margin story.

Group Finance cost +18% YoY to Rs.83.26mn (2025: Rs.70.45mn), a secondary drag (~5% of the PBT decline), against Rs.2,000mn drawn and Rs.1,917.66mn repaid on interest-bearing borrowings within the quarter.

3-for-31 Rights Issue completed May 2026 at Rs.7.50/share raised Rs.507.15mn (Note 6), lifting shares in issue 9.7% to 766,353,136 from 698,733,742; proceeds fully applied to debt settlement -- Rs.262mn to parent Lanka Ventures PLC, Rs.110.99mn combined to DFCC Bank term loans, Rs.134.13mn to an NDB Bank term loan.

Note 5 discloses the Bangladesh associates' FY2025/26 results included Rs.213.8mn of delayed BPDB interest income, which the Group will now recognise in equity-accounted share of profit on a cash-received basis rather than an accrual basis going forward.
key_drivers: Share of earnings from equity accounted investees fell Rs.234.41mn (Group) / Rs.228.13mn (Company) YoY (-60% / -59%), explaining 93.6% / 94.9% of the respective PBT declines -- the dominant driver by a wide margin; no per-associate breakdown disclosed to isolate the cause.

Finance cost rose Rs.12.82mn (Group, +18% YoY) / Rs.10.59mn (Company, +21% YoY), a secondary drag (~5% of the PBT decline) linked to a short-term bridge borrowing (Rs.2,000mn drawn, Rs.1,917.66mn repaid within the quarter) ahead of the May 2026 Rights Issue.

PY comparatives are restated (Note 7, preference-share/NCI reclassification), so part of the YoY movement reflects a changed comparative base rather than pure operating performance -- quantum of restatement not separately disclosed.
